# watchpoint_dashboard (Resource)

An analytics dashboard: a named collection of widgets laid out on a grid, optionally exposed as a public status page.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "watchpoint_dashboard" "example" {
  name        = "Production Overview"
  description = "Top-level production dashboard"
  layout_json = jsonencode([
    { type = "uptime", config = { monitorId = "mon_abc123" }, grid = { x = 0, y = 0, w = 4, h = 2 } },
  ])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable dashboard name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description shown on the dashboard workspace card.
- `folder_id` (String) `watchpoint_dashboard_folder` the dashboard is filed in. Omit for the root. Deleting the folder moves the dashboard up to the folder's parent.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the tenant's default dashboard. Setting it true clears the flag on any other default dashboard. Defaults to `false`.
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether the dashboard is exposed as a public status page. May be blocked by tenant compliance policy. Defaults to `false`.
- `layout_json` (String) JSON-encoded array of widget definitions, each shaped like `{ "type": ..., "config": { ... }, "grid": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 6, "h": 4 } }`. `config` is a free-form per-widget object. Defaults to an empty array (`[]`).
- `owner_group_id` (String) User group (`watchpoint_user_group`) that owns this dashboard. A filter label only; it grants no access.
- `public_slug` (String) URL slug used when the dashboard is public.
- `settings_json` (String) JSON-encoded dashboard-level settings (theme, refresh interval, time range).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Dashboard ID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_dashboard.example dash_001
```
